clue.text: Arguments about river fishes

indicators.note: about means going around, so the arguments wrap round the river

parts.note: spats are petty quarrels or arguments

explanation.surface: Anglers squabble over which river holds the best fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprats are small silvery sea fish of the herring family, so the plural names some fishes.

clue.text: Agreement by which worker must support bad spellers

indicators.note: in a down answer the supporting piece sits underneath, so the worker goes below the spellers

parts.note: a coven is a gathering of witches, who cast wicked spells
the ant is the crossword's usual worker

explanation.surface: A labourer signs an agreement to prop up people who cannot spell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad spellers' looks like poor orthography; it means witches casting evil spells.
explanation.definitionFit: A covenant is a formal binding promise or contract, a solemn agreement.

clue.text: Shows respect, seeing cleft developing within taxonomic group

indicators.note: within says the rearranged letters sit inside the taxonomic group

parts.note: a genus is a rank in biological classification, above species

indicators.note: developing means changing form, so the letters of cleft are reworked

explanation.surface: Someone bows in deference on spotting a split forming in a category of living things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cleft developing' sounds like a geological split forming; 'developing' only reshuffles the five letters, which are opened into the biology rank just after its U.
explanation.definitionFit: To genuflect is to bend the knee in worship or deference, a gesture that shows respect.

clue.text: Arms may be comfortable when raised

indicators.note: in a down answer raising a word makes it read from bottom to top, so comfortable is turned round

parts.note: snug means cosy and comfortable

explanation.surface: Limbs may feel cosy when lifted up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arms' poses as limbs; it means weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: Guns are firearms, and arms is a general word for weapons.

clue.text: Figures as result of reportedly spoilt approaches

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the words are as heard rather than as spelt

parts.note: spoilt means wrecked, and approaches here are angles, ways of tackling something

explanation.surface: Statistics are said to come from botched methods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Figures' suggests numbers; it is shapes. Said aloud, 'wrecked angles' matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Rectangles are four-sided shapes with right angles, examples of geometric figures.

clue.text: Tory leader in tabloid shock

indicators.note: in places the leading letter inside the newspaper's name

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper

indicators.note: a word's leader is its first letter

explanation.surface: A Conservative chief causes a stir in a popular newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid daily.
explanation.definitionFit: To stun is to daze or astonish someone, to give them a shock.

clue.text: Shock term oddly imposed on a university degree

indicators.note: in a down answer something imposed on another is placed above it
oddly means taking the letters in odd positions, first and third

parts.note: MA is a Master of Arts degree

explanation.surface: A shocking term of study is forced on a student taking a degree.
explanation.definitionFit: Trauma is a severe emotional or physical shock, and the clue word names that blow.

clue.text: City firm opening on the outskirts of Rugby

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm
a vent is an opening or outlet

indicators.note: the outskirts of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A business sets up shop on the edge of Rugby, the Warwickshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: Rugby is a town in Warwickshire, near the city of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Coventry is a city in the English Midlands, famous for its cathedral.

clue.text: Manage to get around education's way of doing things

indicators.note: around says the first word wraps itself about the second

parts.note: to procure is to obtain, to manage to get

explanation.surface: An administrator copes with the school system and its methods.
explanation.definitionFit: A procedure is an established method or series of steps, a set way of doing things.

clue.text: Body temperature, more or less

parts.note: or so means approximately, more or less

explanation.surface: A patient's body temperature is roughly normal.
explanation.definitionFit: The torso is the trunk of the human body, without head or limbs.

clue.text: A beautiful woman full of energy approaches

indicators.note: full of means containing, so the energy goes inside the woman

parts.note: Venus, the goddess of love, stands for any beautiful woman
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A lively beauty comes towards someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'approaches' looks like a verb; it is the plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Avenues are ways in or routes of access, so the word can mean approaches or methods.

clue.text: Haircut 100, of course!

parts.note: a ton is slang for a hundred
sure! is an exclamation of agreement, like of course!

explanation.surface: Haircut 100, the 1980s pop group, is named with an emphatic of course.
explanation.walkthrough: Haircut 100 was a British pop band of the early 1980s, so the definition hides in the band name.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonsure is the shaved crown of a monk, a particular style of cutting the hair.

clue.text: Reportedly understand Irish, say

indicators.note: reportedly signals a word heard rather than read

parts.note: to see is to understand, as in I see

explanation.surface: It is said someone can follow the Irish language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Irish' poses as the language; it is the Irish Sea, with 'say' marking it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish Sea, between Britain and Ireland, is one example of a body of salt water.

clue.text: Getting discouraged, seeing how beast may become best

definitions.meaning: the word beast turns into best by dropping its middle letter, the A

explanation.surface: Someone loses spirit watching an animal improve.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of BEAST is its central A; take it away and BEST is left.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose heart is an idiom for becoming dispirited, the state of getting discouraged.

clue.text: Carried euros and held out 500

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: Someone transported euro notes and offered 500 of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges EUROS and HELD into SHOULDERE; D is added.
explanation.definitionFit: To shoulder a load is to carry it on the shoulders, so shouldered means carried.

clue.text: The girl's dietary change is genetic

parts.note: her is the possessive for a girl, the girl's

indicators.note: a change of the letters means rearranging them

explanation.surface: A young woman's new diet is in her genes.
explanation.definitionFit: Hereditary traits are passed down from parents through genes, so the word means inherited or genetic.

clue.text: Time spent in a second room

indicators.note: time spent in something is placed inside it

parts.note: tic stands for tick, a moment or second

explanation.surface: An hour spent in a second room of the house.
explanation.walkthrough: TIC is the setter's spelling of tick, a second; T goes after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: An attic is a room in the roof space of a house.

clue.text: A bread roll and crackers with tea, say, in great supply

parts.note: a bun is a small bread roll

indicators.note: crackers means crazy, so the letters are scrambled
say signals the letter as it is heard

parts.note: tea is pronounced like the letter T

explanation.surface: Bun, biscuits and a cup of tea are plentiful at the table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crackers' looks like biscuits; it rearranges AND into DAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Abundant means plentiful, existing in large quantities, so it is in great supply.

clue.text: Topless work is crude

indicators.note: topless means the top letter, the first, is removed

parts.note: toil is hard work

explanation.surface: Working without a top on is vulgar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crude' poses as vulgar; it is crude oil, petroleum.
explanation.definitionFit: Crude is unrefined petroleum, the raw oil drawn from the ground.

clue.text: Power invested in bank may be answer

indicators.note: invested in means put inside, so power goes within the bank

parts.note: to bank on is to rely on
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: Electricity or influence put into a bank may be the solution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' looks like a noun; it is the verb, to count on.
explanation.definitionFit: A reply is a response, and an answer is likewise a response to a question.

clue.text: Declare in favour of allegation

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
a claim is an assertion or allegation

explanation.surface: Speak up publicly in support of an accusation.
explanation.definitionFit: To proclaim is to announce publicly or officially, which is to declare.

clue.text: A French record with topless models changed and kept under wraps

parts.note: un is the French for a
a disc is a gramophone record

indicators.note: changed signals the remaining letters are rearranged
topless means losing the top letter, the first one

explanation.surface: A French album cover featuring bare-chested models was altered and hushed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' drops the M of MODELS, and 'changed' turns ODELS into LOSED.
explanation.definitionFit: Undisclosed means not revealed or made known, that is kept secret or under wraps.

clue.text: A tyrant's place after poor exam results

indicators.note: after places the place word behind the grades

parts.note: D and E are low exam grades
a spot is a place or location

explanation.surface: A dictator's location after a bad set of results.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after tyrant stands for 'has', linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A despot is a ruler with absolute power, used cruelly, the same as a tyrant.

clue.text: Burt's first to go after Golden Globe

indicators.note: to go after means placed behind the other piece

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold, golden

indicators.note: first means the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Burt Reynolds wins first, after a Golden Globe award.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Golden Globe' is the film award, but the words split: Golden gives OR and Globe is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An orb is a sphere, such as the jewelled ball in regalia, so it is a globe.

clue.text: Exile party outside Northern Ireland

indicators.note: outside means the party goes round the other piece

parts.note: a bash is a party

explanation.surface: A political party is sent away from Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party' suggests a political group; here it is a celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: To banish someone is to send them away from their country, which is to exile them.

clue.text: Question one's place in case of disease

indicators.note: in means placed inside the outer letters
a case is the outside, so the first and last letters

parts.note: I is one, as in Roman numerals, with the s
to put is to place

explanation.surface: A patient queries their position in a medical case.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispute something is to challenge it or call it into doubt, that is question it.

clue.text: House doctor must keep employed

indicators.note: must keep means the letters are held within those words

explanation.surface: Dr House, the TV medic, must stay in work.
explanation.walkthrough: House is the television doctor, but the name only holds letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Used means put to use, so something used has been employed.

clue.text: Bunting festooned in door to landing

indicators.note: festooned in means decorating, sitting inside these words

explanation.surface: Bunting hung across the door leading to the landing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bunting' suggests flag decorations, but it is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The ortolan is a small European songbird of the bunting family.

clue.text: Duty of rising star after Oscar?

indicators.note: after places the rising star behind the O

parts.note: Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: rising in a down answer reads the word upwards

parts.note: the sun is a star

explanation.surface: A film star's obligation after winning an Oscar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oscar' suggests the film award; it is a radio code letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An onus is a burden or responsibility, so it is a duty.

clue.text: Part of aircraft storing old rope

indicators.note: storing means holding inside, so old goes within

parts.note: the nose is the front of an aircraft

explanation.surface: A section of a plane holds a length of old rope.
explanation.definitionFit: A noose is a loop of rope with a running knot, used for hanging.

clue.text: Spain raises doubts about right personal attendants

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain

indicators.note: about means going around, so right goes inside

parts.note: queries means raises doubts

explanation.surface: Spain questions whether certain royal aides are right.
explanation.definitionFit: Equerries are officers of a royal household who attend the monarch personally.
